clauses.reason: Provision 1-101 authorizes the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System to exercise all authority under the Credit Control Act to regulate and control consumer credit. Executive Order No. 12225 restated this provision, effective July 28, 1980, to read: the Board is authorized to establish uniform requirements for changes in terms in open-end credit accounts for consumer credit, with that authorization revoked as of October 31, 1980. Under the strike-and-insert ruling the clause continued, amended, from July 28, 1980 (the substance narrowed from all consumer credit regulation to terms of open-end credit accounts), and it ended by the stated revocation on 1980-10-31, recorded inclusive (the authorization runs through that day; the exclusive reading ends it when October 31 begins). The signing date of Executive Order No. 12225, July 3, 1980, is not the end: that order defers each change to its own stated date.

Provision 1-102 authorizes the Board to regulate and control credit extended by financial intermediaries not subject to certain reserve-requirement laws that are primarily engaged in extending short-term credit. Executive Order No. 12225 revokes the authorization granted by Section 1-102 of this order as of August 11, 1980, so the first end is 1980-08-11. The date is stated by that order and is not the signing date, July 3, 1980.

Provision 1-103 authorizes the Board to regulate and control credit extended to commercial banks that are not members of the Federal Reserve System in the form of managed liabilities. Executive Order No. 12225 revokes the authorizations granted by Sections 1-103 and 1-104 of this order as of July 28, 1980, so the first end is 1980-07-28.

Provision 1-104 authorizes the Board to prescribe record-keeping requirements with respect to all forms of credit under Section 206(4) of the Credit Control Act. Executive Order No. 12225 revokes the authorizations granted by Sections 1-103 and 1-104 of this order as of July 28, 1980, so the first end is 1980-07-28.

Provision 1-105 defines the terms consumer credit, financial intermediaries, short-term credit, commercial banks and managed liabilities by reference to Federal Reserve regulations. Executive Order No. 12225 restated it, effective July 28, 1980, to define only consumer credit and open-end credit; under the strike-and-insert ruling the clause continued, amended. The provision gives no command; it only defines terms used by the authorizations in Sections 1-101 through 1-104. After Executive Order No. 12225 revoked Sections 1-102 through 1-104 and 1-106 and set the last remaining authorization, amended Section 1-101, to be revoked as of October 31, 1980, no authorization remained for the definitions to serve. This is an inference from the structure of the two orders, not an express revocation of this section; the first end is recorded as 1980-10-31, the date the last authorization it served was revoked, and the reviewer should treat it as a reasoned dependent lapse.

Provision 1-106 says the authorizations granted by the order remain in effect for an indefinite period and until revoked by the President. Executive Order No. 12225 revokes Section 1-106 of this order without stating a later date, so the revocation is treated as effective on the signing date, July 3, 1980; the alternative reading from Federal Register publication, July 7, 1980, is not a stated effective date. The first end is 1980-07-03. The revocation removes the statement of duration only; the authorizations it described were then ended by their own stated revocations.

conflict_resolutions.STATED_EFFECTIVE_DATE_DIFFERS: Executive Order No. 12225 was signed July 3, 1980 but states later effective dates for each of its provisions (July 28, August 11 and October 31, 1980). The stated provision dates control the first ends recorded here; the signing date controls only the revocation of Section 1-106, which states no later date.
